result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks and buildings directly abutting the walkway, creating a consistent urban edge. However, the wide roadway with multiple lanes and lack of marked crossings or traffic calming measures prioritizes vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parking
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb create significant visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross the street and for drivers to see them.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbsides throughout the visible block

hazards.name: Lack of Designated Crossings
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks or pedestrian-oriented signage over a long stretch of road forces pedestrians to cross at unprotected locations.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire roadway visible in the foreground and mid-ground

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add high-visibility marked crosswalks and pedestrian warning signs to designate safe crossing points.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Plant street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and moving traffic.

result.summary: The image shows a typical urban residential street lined with row houses and parallel parking. While sidewalks are present and continuous, the environment lacks dedicated traffic calming measures or physical buffers like street trees between pedestrians and the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of traffic calming
hazards.description: The straight, wide roadway lacks physical measures to discourage speeding in a residential context.

hazards.name: Minimal vertical buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk lacks vertical elements like trees or bollards to protect pedestrians from potential vehicle incursions beyond the parked cars.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Adding street trees would provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the street while helping to slow traffic.

interventions.title: Speed Cushions
interventions.description: Implementing speed cushions would help regulate vehicle speeds to safer levels for a residential block.

result.summary: The image depicts a standard urban street with multi-story buildings situated directly at the sidewalk edge. While the environment includes signalized intersections with marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals, it lacks dedicated bicycle infrastructure and physical buffers between the walkway and moving traffic.

hazards.name: Visibility obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb near the intersection may obstruct the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street approaching the intersection.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway at the intersection increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic without a refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: The intersection of 16th St visible in the background.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide shade, improve the pedestrian experience, and naturally encourage slower driving speeds through vertical enclosure.
